verdict.rationale: Databricks documents OpenSharing, a first-party secure data-sharing platform for sharing data and AI assets with users outside your organization, even if they don't use Databricks. A Marketplace that includes dataset listings supports this. The evidence does not explicitly say shares are live or avoid copying data or building export pipelines, so the zero-copy part of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that shared datasets are live and not copied, details on sharing to another Databricks account versus a non-Databricks recipient, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can share live datasets with another account or organization without copying data or building an export pipeline

citations.quote: OpenSharing is the secure data sharing platform in Databricks that lets you share data and AI assets with users outside your organization, regardless of whether they use Databricks.
Listings include datasets, AI models, notebooks, apps, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
publish offerings that Databricks customers can discover, evaluate, and connect with directly from their workspace
